component.name: Parley
component.summary: Private voice, video and screen-share calls between friends

description.p: Parley lets two or three friends call each other directly: voice, webcams and screen sharing with sound, all at once. There are no accounts and no servers to set up, and calls are end-to-end encrypted.

ul.li: Add a friend once by sharing a code or scanning a QR code
Group calls that survive someone dropping out, with one-click rejoin
Share your whole desktop's sound or just chosen apps, without echoing the call
Echo cancellation and noise suppression

screenshot.caption: A call with a shared screen

ul.li: Pictures: give yourself or anyone an image, or letters or a symbol on a colour or gradient (GNOME style). They stay on your computer
Settings → Appearance → Pictures: key patterns or GNOME-style initials for people without a picture
Group owners: whoever creates a group owns it (crown in its member list) and can right-click a member to remove them; removed people can't rejoin with the group code
Light, dark, or follow the system: Settings → General → Appearance
Option to hide the #tags after names
Adwaita icons built in, so Parley looks the same on KDE and other desktops; the phone icon now faces the familiar way

Replace my identity (Settings → General → Privacy): for when your code got out. You get a new code and the old one stops working at once; friends and group members are moved over automatically as they come online, and nobody else learns the new code
Group chats list all their members at the bottom of the sidebar, friends included, with their status
User info works for group members who aren't your friends
The sidebar stays docked beside everything, calls and chats included; only its button hides it, and that choice is remembered
Your name at the top of the sidebar takes you to the home page; during a call the home page has Return to call
Group chats list the members who aren't your friends at the bottom of the sidebar, with their status; click the group's header to jump there, a member for their info, or + to add them
Fill-window mode: the call controls float over the stream and fade with its name and LIVE badge after 4 seconds without mouse movement; the "Press F or Esc" hint disappears after 2 seconds
The F, M and D shortcuts work in a call even when the sidebar has keyboard focus
No more empty grey strip beside a call after closing its chat panel
The chat no longer jumps when sending a message during a call
Text chat with friends and groups, peer to peer and end-to-end encrypted, in a Discord-like view; messages to someone offline are delivered when you're both online
Chat beside a call, unread counts, notifications and clickable links
The installer moves your identity over and removes the old launcher when switching between native and Flatpak installs
Unique pictures (identicons) and name tags like alice#f3a7, derived from each identity's key, so people with the same name can be told apart
User info for each contact: full key and contact code, date added, status and Parley version
Parley's version shown at the top of the sidebar; friends' versions in User info and on their call tile
Screen sharing works when the screen's GPU frames can't be imported (seen with some AMD setups): capture switches to shared memory automatically
Black bars around video instead of grey
A stream's overlay (name, LIVE badge, buttons) and the pointer fade out after a few seconds without mouse movement, like a video player
Group calls show who's in them in the sidebar, even before you join: avatars, a red LIVE badge while someone shares their screen, and mute/deafen icons
A stream can fill the window (F, double-click or its button); F11 toggles full screen
Screen share at 480p too, and 24, 30, 60 fps or a custom frame rate
Adaptive streaming: when the connection can't keep up, a stream's bitrate drops at once to keep motion smooth, then climbs back
Full-screen view for a stream or person (button, right-click menu, or double-click; Esc exits)
Choose screen-share resolution and frame rate independently
Closing the window keeps the call going in the tray
Sounds when people join and leave
A thicker, glowing speaking ring that shows over video
"Hear yourself" mic test in Settings, delayed a second
Voice Isolation, Studio and Custom input profiles, with neural noise suppression (RNNoise) that removes keyboards, desk knocks and chewing
Input sensitivity: automatic, or a manual threshold with a live mic meter
Automatic gain keeps voices at a steady, comfortable loudness
Online, Do Not Disturb and Invisible status, shown on your friends
Right-click a stream or person for volume, mute and stop watching
Smoother audio on choppy Wi-Fi; narrow windows fit on screen
